content: Take this medication exactly as prescribed by your doctor. It is essential to maintain a consistent level of the drug in your body for optimal effectiveness. Administer the medication at evenly spaced intervals. Do not take more or less than the prescribed dose, and do not discontinue use, even for a short period, unless directed by your doctor. Stopping the medication prematurely may lead to an increase in the virus, make the infection more resistant to treatment, or exacerbate side effects. Common side effects may include headache, fatigue, dizziness, or nausea. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. If you experience any unusual symptoms, contact your doctor for medical advice. Before starting entecavir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you are sure you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages, as alcohol may worsen liver problems. To reduce the risk of transmitting hepatitis B to others, always use effective barrier methods (such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams) during all sexual activity. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It is not known whether this medication prevents the transmission of the hepatitis B virus from mother to baby. Additionally, it is unclear if this medication passes into breast milk. If you have HIV, breastfeeding may transmit the virus to your baby. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose, if someone has severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests (such as liver function tests and viral load measurements) should be performed regularly to monitor your progress and check for side effects. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Keep the medication in its original carton to protect it from light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
